notes.title: Update 1.67: Optimization (pretty large scale)
notes.notes:
I took steps to reduce both CPU and GPU requirements for the game. 

CPU:

When the Update thread drops frames it will reduce how fast the AI updates for the units. They are minor adjustments, but it should give you about 20% more "reach" for your CPU.

GPU:

When the Draw thread drops frames the game will start reducing units being drawn. Selected units will always draw, as will military units and cart pushers. However all the rest of the units will start to be left of the scene. This seems to give your CPU about 25% greater "reach".


IF you see any bugs (they should be all display bugs if any, as I played for ~10 hours with the new systems and the game still worked great), please let me know.

Worst case scenario is (as far as I can tell) will be that a unit wont be displayed that should otherwise be displayed...

notes.title: Update 1.47: Basic Goods production Flow work, and balancing
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone,

So I spent the last few days working towards a better flow for most of the basic goods production pipelines. There have been reductions in workers needed, a rise in carrying capacity for cart pushers, and much more. They are lots of little change that add up to a much better flow :) 

- The "Unobtained desires" has been split into "Desires Basic Goods" and "Desires Food Variety". This should help to better explain what is needed.
- Tailor Shops now only need 2 tailors, each tailors now work fast enough to make up it. This should have no effect on production capacity, but reduces total population required.
- Weaving shops now only need 2 weavers, each weavers now work fast enough to make up it. This should have no effect on production capacity, but reduces total population required.
- Butcher Shops now only need 2 butchers, each butchers now work fast enough to make up it. This should have no effect on production capacity, but reduces total population required.
- Sheep Farms now only need 3 Shepherds, each shepherds now work fast enough to make up it. This should have no effect on production capacity, but reduces total population required.
- Pottery Huts now only need 2 pottery workers, each pottery worker now work fast enough to make up it. This should have no effect on production capacity, but reduces total population required.
- Furniture Factories now only need 2 furniture workers, each furniture workers now work fast enough to make up it. This should have no effect on production capacity, but reduces total population required.
- Doubled the amount of wood that can be chopped from trees.
- Wool production has been halved, but the requirement to make cloth has also be halved, and the trade value has been doubled... The net effect should be to reduce the cloging of your warehouses, it trades for more (same number = more money), and to make it easier for cart pushers to deal with it.
- Cart pushers now have a carrying capacity of 5.
- Lumber is now produced more quickly.
- Furnature is now produced more quickly.
- Cloths are now produced more quickly.
- Carrying speed increased.
- Furniture is now produced 2 at time, and costs 5 lumber per 2 down from 3 per.
- food lasts a bit longer.

Lastly,

If you are enjoying the game (or at least like the direction it is going), please put a review up for the game as it really helps me out. Positive reviews causes steams algorithm to send more traffic to the game, which in turn allows me to spend more money on assets and sounds for the game.

notes.title: Update 1.46: Desire system 2.0, Level 3 housing, rebalancing, and some major bug fixes.
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone,

I hope you all had a great week last week, and happy belated Thanks Giving for all you USA peoples! So this is one of my biggest patches I have ever done for this game (normally they are many small patches, rather than a few large ones), but this is a big change and it required time.

Desires system 2.0:

Desires are no longer based on the home that the unit is living in, but rather based on their desired home. This should make it more beneficial to upgrade homes (less negatives all at once). Desires now give +2 happiness for each desire they have in their inventory, and -1 for any desire that is missing. I have been putting a ton of testing into this system, but it will requires some tweaking to perfect. This system allows for much higher happiness of well made cities, but is more punishing for poorly made cities.

Level 3 housing:

Most of the jobs that wanted level 2 housing now want level 3 housing. In general finishing workers, architects, priests, and constables want level 2 housing now. This should require many many more houses to be upgrades, as a result the upgrade costs for houses have been cut in half.

Patch Notes (I will be honest some of the minor changes didnt make it on the list):

- Added A starving overlay. Red means at least 1 person is starving that lives there.
- The "Obtained Desires" buff has been fully reworked. Now it will check daily to see if the units desires are met, and then grant a +2 happiness buff for all met desires, and -1 desires for all unmet desires. This will allow a much higher happiness cap in well run cities, but it will reduce happiness for poorly run cities.
- Desires are no longer based on the house that the individual is living in, rather they are now based on what level house they desire to live in... This will push the users towards upgrading housing appropriately.
- Almost all professions that required level 2 housing previously, now require level 3 housing. The exception to this is priests who will remain at 2.
- Architects wages have been raised to 6 from 5.
- Architects now desire level 2 housing.
- Constables now desire level 2 housing.
- Game Operators now desire level 2 housing.
- Blacksmiths now desire level 2 housing.
- Furniture Workers now desire level 2 housing.
- Tailors now desire level 2 housing.
- Bowyer Workers now desire level 2 housing.
- Mint Workers now desire level 2 housing.
- Pottery Workers now desire level 2 housing.
- Wine Workers now desire level 2 housing.
- Butchers now desire level 2 housing.
- Level 2 housing upgrade cost reduced to 25 Denarii and 2 wood from 50 Denarii and 3 wood.
- The penalty for wanting clean water for level 2 houses has been reduced to -1 happiness from -2 happiness.
- Wealthier people now eat a bit more food.
- Residence of level 1 housing no longer desire basic items.
- The "Paid On Time" happiness buff has been removed, as it was no longer needed, and always present in the current format.
- Town Halls now start with 20 Wood, 10 Bricks, and 4 Lumber in custom games. This should help get your city going early.
- Grapes now produce more slowly.
- Sheep now produce faster.
- Clothing now produces faster.
- Clothing now costs 5 cloth for 2 Clothing, down from 3 cloth for 1 clothing.
- Wool Thread now produces faster.
- Cloth now produces faster.
- Reservoirs range is now 8 up from 7.
- Doctors office range is now 4 up from 3, but the building now wants 3 doctors up from 2.
- Swords now require 5 iron to make down from 6.
- Markets can now store 125 items up from 100, the upgrade has also been increased to 150 from 125.
- Wants Education debuff has been reduced to -1 happiness from -2 happiness.
- Fixed a bug in the "not accepting" feature that could allow the resource in.
- Fixed a bug in the shopping AI that could result in a unit not buying something when they otherwise should have (this will reduce starving in large cities).


If you guys are enjoying the game, or at least the direction it is going, please take a second and put up a review for the game. Positive reviews help boost traffic, and thus will increase how much I can spend on the game. Thanks in advance!

- New Stat Tab: Imperial Tab, This tab will show all imperial requests, and any other imperial bits that get added over time.
- Fixed the width on one of the alerts for Ceres.

notes.notes:
Hey Everyone,

Today I added the Doctors Office, which is a small building that gives out health services. Doctors require education. Most of the the patch however is bug fixes and balance changes. - New Building: Doctors Office, Doctors Offices provide better health through healing sick people. Doctors do require a basic education (which will be raised to a secondary education when I get that in). Doctors offices are a 1x1 building with a short range.

- I added more info to the building info menu of houses. This should help to clearify what the house desires and what it is getting.
- Trade routes now have real names :)
- Trade routes now have differing costs (this only affects custom Games).
- Thread maker now makes 8 thread per sheep, up from 1.
- Reservoirs how have 7 range up from 5.
- Reservoirs no longer have the working animations play.
- Fixed a bug in the bath house that made its spread not accurate.
- Mints and most trade goods now yield more money on lower difficulties.
- Farms now produced 10% more food.
- I spent Spent some time optimizing the game for larger cities, overall the game should use about 8% less resources when cities get large (I will do more in the future, but this shoudl help smooth things out a bit).
- Fixed a bug where the AI was continuing to increase its population even when it did not need to (I believe this is what was causing the level 5 lag).
- The tooltips no longer state a level number on the campaign levels, instead they now state if the level is Peaceful or a Battle.


Lastly,

notes.title: Update 1.34: Reservoirs, Aqueducts, Fountains, and more!
notes.notes:

I realize its been longer than normal between patches. This system took quite a bit longer than I expected... That being said you now need fountains which in turn need water from a reservoir in order to keep houses level 2 and above happy. I also added the Bath House (more health services coming soon), which will be needed for level 2 and above houses also. Having more health services than are required will gain you happiness (Formula: house level - 1 = needed health services). So a level 1 house with access to baths will have +1 happiness.

I also added a few storage alerts, as it seems that is a step people seem to be missing when they are having trouble with the game. A few debuffs have been changed, and a few buildings have been added to level 4 and 5 of the campaign that if used well should make both levels easier.

Localization:

I plan to have German and French in on Thursday, right before launch. These 2 languages are all I could afford at this point, but I hope to add more as time goes on.


Patch Notes:

- New Building: Reservoir, Reservoirs store water for use in your city. Reservoirs must be placed by water or attached to Aqueducts.
- New Building: Aqueducts, Aqueducts transport water between Reservoirs.
- New Building: Fountain, The Fountain provides clean water to a specific area. Clean water is good enough for all citizens. Needs access to Reservoirs.
- New Building: Bath House, Bath Houses provide better health through cleanliness, and waste waste disposal. Needs access to Reservoirs.
- New Alert: Low Storage, this alert happens the first time your storage is over 95% full. This alert should help you not forget to build storage (happens to me from time to time).
- New Alert: Low Food Storage, this alert happens when you have a few farms but no Granaries. This alert will only happen once, but it is designed to make sure people know they need food storage.
- Alerts should not longer bombard you right away when you load a game.
- False alerts should no longer go off right after a load.
- Fixed a bug when loading a game, that left people in a bugged state until their stamina ran out.
- The Dice House in now available to build on campaign levels 3-5 (everything after that has access to everything already). This should make it easier to get your happiness numbers up.
- The debuff for an undesirable home has been increased from -2 to -3 happiness.
- New debuff for level 2 houses: "Wants Clean Water", which means that they want water from a fountain. If they have access to a well the dubuff is -2, but if they have access to no water it is -4.
- New debuff for level 2 houses(and above): "Wants Health Services" which is a debuff of -1 happiness if there are no health services available to the home. You need 1 health service for each level home 2 and above.
- New Buff, "Healthy" which is a +1 happiness buff for every extra health service that a home has access to.

notes.title: Update 1.32: Bridges, and Muggings
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone,

The Main bits today are Bridges, and the Mugging event. Bridges are pretty straight forward with the exception of you cant build 2 bridges right next to each other, and they can only go a maximum of 5 water spaces (also bridges may not line up 100% perfectly with each segment, I will try to get this worked out next week). Muggings happen when your people are unhappy (individual people not the average), and can not happen before the 20th day. Muggings also have a cooldown, so you wont just go from rich to bankrupt in no time. To see which areas of your city are unhappy I also added a happiness overlay.

The bridge will allow you to build on 2 sides of a river much more effectively, and the mugging event will finally give you a hard reason to keep your happiness up. Both additions should have a substantial effect on gameplay :)

Patch Notes:

- New Building: Bridge, The bridge will allow for faster travel over water. Bridges cost 25 per segment. People can still travel through water, but bridges make it much more feasible to build on both sides of a river.
- New Overlay: Happiness Overlay. The happiness overlay will give you an at a glance view of the average happiness of each home. Keep in mind that just because the average is good, does not mean their are not individual issues...
- Muggings of your tax collectors can now happen when your people are unhappy. This effect is lessened by Constables. The mugging severity scales with your city, and can not take place in the first 20 days.
- minor text changes in various places.
- Added a building collapse animation.
- Granary now shows how full it is by how many windows are filled.
- Fixed a bug where if you removed your builders before you built any houses, they would not retake their jobs and nothing could be built.
- New immigrants will no longer take jobs until they have a home. This fixes a bug that could make your people work infinitely without resting.

Next up:

I am currently working on the rest of the water and health system. I hope to have them done by Friday next week along with level 6.

notes.title: Update 1.28: Campaign Level 4
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone,

As mentioned last patch today's patch includes level 4. It shows you how to get a Mint working, and expects a bit higher stats to finish the level. But the biggest part of this patch is actually people moving homes when needed. This will happen automatically, and will allow well planned out cities to become super efficient. However planning where your upgraded housing is located has started to become a thing as people desiring level 2 (or higher when its in game) housing will move to the closest level 2 housing slot to their work (even if it is the furthest house away). The last change to the housing system is that people will only immigrate to fill level 1 housing slots, so you will need to have at least some level 1 housing in order to add people to your city. 

This polish step of the housing system is a great example of how I want to add depth to systems. I want your choices to matter, and I want players to see the difference in well planed out cities. 


Patch Notes:

- Level 4: Bobium, This is a peaceful city mainly focused on getting a Mint working and supplementing trade.
- An achievement has been added for beating level 4.
- New Overlay: House Upgrade Overlay, This overlay shows which houses have residence that want better housing.
- People will now only immigrate if there are open spaces level 1 houses (tents).
- People will now automatically move to houses of the appropriate level. But be careful, they will do so even if the house is very far from work.
- People will now automatically move to houses that are much closer to their work IF they live far from work (the will not move if they feel they are already close enough). This should help to make your cities run much more efficiently, however if you decentralize to much you may find it hard to keep your people happy due to lack of amenities.
- Trading posts now have their sales scroll over the building just like the Market does.
- Deities now accumulate mood score more slowly.
- Fixed a bug in immigration spawn points.
- Holding down "Shift" now causes scroll speeds to double.

I really hope you guys enjoy level 4, let me know what you think so that I can make adjustments as needed.

- Sheep takes slightly longer to produce.
- Cloth takes slightly less time to produce.
- A few resources have had their trade values slightly increased.

Whats next:

With the number of buildings now soaring to 38 (up from about 20 when EA started), and more systems in place I am going to start putting more focus on depth of each system, rather than the current main focus of getting MORE EVERYTHING in.

This does not mean that more buildings/resources/systems arnt coming, but the pace of new buildings/resources/systems is going to slow down a bit in order to make time for expanding on what is already there.

Some examples are:

- More gods
- More god powers
- Shops like the Pottery Hut having more than 1 resource to make.
- Some of the negative effects that you will need to keep at bay, like people stealing from tax collectors, and lighting buildings on fire when they are unhappy, etc...
- Level 3 houses.
- Religious and Entertainment buildings taking in specific resources that will boost their range. (an example would be the Theater having access to clay masks will boost its range 1 further).



Whats the next system?

I recently commissioned the art for the water and health system. This system will go in in stages but it should bring more depth with each stage.

When is level 4 coming?

I would say I am about 70% done with level 4, and I HOPE to have it in on Tuesday's patch. So if you want to have access to level 4 when it launches make sure to beat 1-3 before then.

notes.title: Update 1.25: Entertainment System, 4 new Buildings, and 2 new Resources!
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone!

This is a big one today! We got a new system, 4 new buildings, 2 new resources, and some balance changes to boot! The Entertainment System is working well so far. Its very similar to the Religion system in how it works, but it really adds a lot to the planning aspect of the city. The 2 buildings that entertain your people are the Gladiator Pit, and the Theater. Aside from that we have 2 new resource buildings in the Thread Maker, and Weaving Shop. The Thread maker produces Wool, and the Weaving Shop produces Cloth. Thread is a basic resource, and Cloth is an middle tier resource.

Patch Notes:

- New System: Entertainment. The Entertainment system works similarly to the religious system in that it is area based, but rather than dealing with the gods it has double the effect on your people's happiness.
- New Building: Glaidator Pit. The Gladiator Pit provides entertainment for a large area. However Glaidators do tend to die from time to time... The Glaidator pit is a 3x3 building.
- New Building: Theater. The Theater provides entertainment for a medium area. Thesbians require a basic education. The Theater is a 2x2 building.
- New Building: Thread Maker, This buildings spins Wool from Sheep.
- New Building: Weaving Shop, This building weaves Cloth from Wool.
- New Resource: Wool, Wool comes from sheep (7 wool per sheep), and is a basic resource costing just 1/2 (local/trade). Wool is used to make other items.
- New Resource: Cloth, Cloth is made from Wool (4 wool makes 1 cloth), and it is an intermediate level resource costing 6/12 (local/trade). Cloth will be used to make other items at a later date.
- Fixed a bug where opening trade routes could give you money rather than taking it.
- Base Wages for most workshops have been set to 5 up from 4.
- Base Wages for most Finishing Shops have been set to 6 up from 5.
- To offset the base wage increases finished goods have had their trade values increased by 1 or 2 per unit.
- Most production shops are now hold more resources. 40 of the ingrediant(s) (up from 20), and 15 of the product (up from 10). This should help to smooth out production.
- Demolish now stays active until you right click, or toggle it off.
- Fixed a bug in updateing the gods that allowed for them to get mad before you could even start building.
- Swapped AI Player's AI to its own thread. This should help to negate some of the issues with lag in the later game. If you notice anything strange, please let me know, but my tests have showed promising results.
- In the build menu "Social" have been changed to "Amenities" as it is more accurate. (thanks for the feedback)
- Trade routes now have 3-4 items in each segment up from 2-3.
- Added an entertainment overlay.
- All the Mines now only have 4 miners. The production requirements where also dropped by 20% to make up for this.
- All the Farm now only have 4 Farmers. The production requirements where also dropped by 20% to make up for this.
- Reduced some building build times. 


I hope you guys like the patch! Let me know what you think! Feed back on new systems is very important!

The 2 buildings that entertain your people are the Gladiator Pit, and the Theater. Aside from that we have 2 new resource buildings in the Thread Maker, and Weaving Shop. The Thread maker produces Wool, and the Weaving Shop produces Cloth. Thread is a basic resource, and Cloth is an middle tier resource.

Patch Notes:

- New System: Entertainment. The Entertainment system works similarly to the religious system in that it is area based, but rather than dealing with the gods it has double the effect on your people's happiness.
- New Building: Glaidator Pit. The Gladiator Pit provides entertainment for a large area. However Glaidators do tend to die from time to time... The Glaidator pit is a 3x3 building.
- New Building: Theater. The Theater provides entertainment for a medium area. Thesbians require a basic education. The Theater is a 2x2 building.
- New Building: Thread Maker, This buildings spins Wool from Sheep.
- New Building: Weaving Shop, This building weaves Cloth from Wool.
- New Resource: Wool, Wool comes from sheep (7 wool per sheep), and is a basic resource costing just 1/2 (local/trade). Wool is used to make other items.
- New Resource: Cloth, Cloth is made from Wool (4 wool makes 1 cloth), and it is an intermediate level resource costing 6/12 (local/trade). Cloth will be used to make other items at a later date.
- Fixed a bug where opening trade routes could give you money rather than taking it.
- Base Wages for most workshops have been set to 5 up from 4.
- Base Wages for most Finishing Shops have been set to 6 up from 5.
- To offset the base wage increases finished goods have had their trade values increased by 1 or 2 per unit.
- Most production shops are now hold more resources. 40 of the ingrediant(s) (up from 20), and 15 of the product (up from 10). This should help to smooth out production.
- Demolish now stays active until you right click, or toggle it off.
- Fixed a bug in updateing the gods that allowed for them to get mad before you could even start building.
- Swapped AI Player's AI to its own thread. This should help to negate some of the issues with lag in the later game. If you notice anything strange, please let me know, but my tests have showed promising results.
- In the build menu "Social" have been changed to "Amenities" as it is more accurate. (thanks for the feedback)
- Trade routes now have 3-4 items in each segment up from 2-3.
- Added an entertainment overlay.
- All the Mines now only have 4 miners. The production requirements where also dropped by 20% to make up for this.
- All the Farm now only have 4 Farmers. The production requirements where also dropped by 20% to make up for this.
- Reduced some building build times. 


I hope you guys like the patch! Let me know what you think! Feed back on new systems is very important!

notes.title: Update 1.23: Butcher Shop, Meat, Balance and Polish!
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone!

Bullet point wise this is on of the larger recent patches, it has a bit of everything in it. The Butcher shop converts sheep to meat, and meat is a 3/6 t2 food (meaning that t2 houses want it). Grapes have been moved to a t3 food in perpetration for an expanded housing system at a later date. Lots of small balance changes have made it in as well as some bug fixes, and a touch of polish work to boot.

Unfortunately the 1 thing this patch doesn't have is the campaign. So far I have about 1.5 levels done, but I have completed all of the pipeline work as well as most of the different tutorial functionality. When I have 3 levels done I will get it out to you guys. Sorry for the delay, but the tutorial functionality kinda kicked my butt. After the initial 3 levels come out I expect to have an average of about 1 level per week created.

Patch Notes:

- New Building: Butcher Shop. The Butcher Shop will convert 1 sheep to 3 meat.
- New Resource: Meat. Meat will be a tier 2 food (level 2 houses want it). Meat costs 3/6 (local/trade).
- Bowyer shops now have 3 Bow Worker slots down from 4.
- Bows now require 30% less work to create (this is to balance out the above).
- Blacksmith shops now have 3 Blacksmith slots down from 4.
- Swords now require 30% less work to create (this is to balance out the above).
- Wine now requires 4 grapes down from 5.
- Wine has had its value reduced to 20/40 (local/trade) down from 25/50.
- Grapes have been bumped up from level 2 food, to level 3 food (meat will now fill the role of the desired level 2 house food). This will have the effect of people being less likely to spend to much on grades (meat is cheaper than grapes), as well as prepair for level 3 housing.
- Sheep farms now produce 2 sheep per cycle.
- Sheep prices have been reduced to 6/12 down from 8/15.
- Vineyards now produce 5 units of grapes down from 6
- Added how many items are produced to the production area of the Building Info menu as well as to the building buy tooltip (for instance the farm will show 8 grain being produced now).
- Fixed a rare crash having to do with resources being spent.
- Fixed a bug where sometimes the first time a new resource was taken to a warehouse it would only create the slot but not add the resources.
- The happiness tooltip now shows your populations top 3 issues up from 2.
- Mouse Input should no longer click through other active programs and affect the game.
- Keyboard input should no longer affect the game when the game is not the active window.
- The affect that snow has on farming has been reduced.
- Slightly increased the speed that builders build.
- Slightly reduced the "Carrying Resource" speed penalty.
- Market's storage now looks like warehouse storage does.
- Fixed a bug where Granaries seemed to randomly turn away new goods...
- Fixed a crash that has to do with flooding.


I really hope you guys are able to "feel" the difference all these changes are having. I know for me the amount of time I can play without having to stop and fix something is growing substantially. Thank you all for pushing me to make things better, it does help to know that spending the extra time working on the game will help make your experiences better.

If you guys are enjoying the game, or at least like where it is going, please take a minute and put up a review for the game. Every little bit helps, and I would love to get a bit more traffic so that I can afford to have another batch of sounds and music made for the game. Thanks in advance!

notes.title: Update 1.21b: Clean up and some polish.
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone,

Most of the update for today is things that have been lingering for quite some time, and I needed to hammer them out. I also tried to get in some of the feedback changes that have been requested. The major things in the patch are the scrolling of sold items over the market place, let me know what you think about it. I have been trying to come up with a way to give a clue about how the market system works without the users having to read a tutorial (which I will also put in later), and someone sent in this idea. Overall I really like it so far, but I want to know what you guys think.

Also The spiting of the trade prices is minor right now, but it will make balancing the desires system much easier in the future. I really tried to keep it to 1 prices, but it has been very cumbersome and I am not even 1/2 way into that system...


- Resources bought from the market now scroll over the market. This should help people to see what is being bought at a glance, as well as make it more obvious that the market is doing the selling.
- The trade system pricing has been divided into a local price and an export price. In general the export price is double what the local price is. Long term this will make the game much easier to balance.
- Bricks now require 3 clay down from 4.
- Bricks now have a trade value of 16 down from 20.
- The Building Info menu for houses now tells you which gods that residence in that building have access to.
- Fixed a bug in the immigration location.
- Cleaned up a few bugs in the pathing AI.
- Fixed a bug at the start of the game in which the builders would stop working after the first house was built and go rest (even though they didnt need rest yet).d
- Made the highlight for buildings a bit less harsh.
- Level 2 houses now highlight properly.
- The building sites now highlight properly.
- Fixed a bug where a flood could destroy your town hall. This is the only building that should not be able to be destroyed by a flood...
- I started the process of converting text to files rather than static strings. This process will allow the game to be translated more easily. Please keep and eye out for bugs in this process and I will get them fixed.

I am still waiting on art for the sheep resources, but if I have them in time then I will get them in Friday.

The campaign continues to make progress, and the goal is still to have the first few levels out this month :)

Keep me posted with feedback guys. I really cant stress how helpful the feedback is (good, bad, or neutral). If there is info you need or something is bothering you please let me know! But if you like something it is just as important to let me know so that i dont go all renegade and "fix" a problem that isn't there. A ton of the feedback I have gotten from the community has made it into the game, some of it is still sitting on a to do list, and then there is some that I dont think will fit into the game. 

You guys are awesome and thank all for being as involved as you guys have been!

notes.title: Update 1.21: Bowyer, Archery Range, and Archers
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone!

Today we have 2 new buildings and 1 new military unit. The Bowyer makes bows from lumber, and the Archery range trains Archers which are are basic ranged unit. On top of the new buildings and units I have spend a decent amount of time reworking the Military unit's AIs. As far as I can see they are objectively better than they were before (I cant find anything that is worse about them), but they still have lots of space to improve. Some feedback on the military unit AIs would be very helpful.

Currently I am about a week behind where I wanted to be, but progress is definitely being made. I made really good headway on the campaign this week, and I am pretty optimistic that the first 3 levels will be ready this month. That being said I want to set some expectations for those 3 levels. Essentially they are gonna be tutorial levels (really the first 5 levels are gonna be tutorial levels), that try to teach you how to play the game. For those of you that already have the hang of the game, this may not be very exciting, but it is a must in order for the game to succeed. After those first 5 levels the campaign will start to branch out and become much more varied and interesting.


Patch Notes:

- New Building: Bowyer, The Bowyer produces Bows from Lumber.
- New Building: Archery Range, This building trains archers. :)
- New Unit: Archer, This unit is trained at the Archery Range and is a basic ranged unit for the Romans. While overall weaker than the Legionnaire, the archer is normally able to attack more due to not having to chase a target down as often.
- Vastly improved the military Unit AI for picking a target.
- Minor readjustments to resource values (some up and some down).
- Fixed the draw point of mountains, this should help units not inappropriately draw behind them.
- Fixed a bug allowing units health to go above full when they eat (eating is how they heal btw).
- fixed a bug having to do with loading Rally Points.
- fixed a bug in the constables AI that could cause them to dance around their target.

What is next?

I need to work on the AI players quite a bit. I had hoped to get to some of it this week, but I didnt quite get to it yet.

Also, provided that the art comes in in time I should have some new resources for you all as follows:

- Sheep (from a sheep farm)
- Meat (from sheep, via a Butcher)
- Wool (from sheep, via a Wool Maker [If someone has a better name for this please let me know, I have been looking for one, but cant find one])

More items will come from a sheep later but I highly doubt enough art will come in to get more than that in next week.

notes.title: Update 1.20: gods and their powers!
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone,

Today we finally have god powers! I started with 1 basic power in 2 different strengths, and both positive and negative versions of that power for each god. More powers will be coming, as I hope to have 5+ unique powers (not counting strengths and positive/negative variations) per god. Right now the system works based on the % of the population that has access to a temple of each god. This builds up into the mood score of the god, from there the mood consolidates into points (happy or mad faces), and then the god uses those points to bless you or curse you. You will need 50% + (5% * difficulty level) coverage to keep the god happy, any higher will gain you favor, and less will upset the god over time. As points are gained it started to take more mood score to get points, however mood score is affected by population, so as your city grows in will increase the speed at which you gain/loose mood score.

Right now it is pretty easy to keep the gods happy, but as more gods get added it will become more difficult to fit all of the different temples around your populations. I fully expect that this system needs tweaking, so please let me know what you think, and I will keep tweaking this system until it is balanced. Right now I have the rates of the spells increased so that you can see them in action, I will cut their rates down in the next patch.

Patch Notes.

- New Ceres god Power: Lesser Blessing of food, This power will give you 25% of your possible food stores in warehouses and farms (this power will not fill warehouses that have the food resources turned off).
- New Ceres god Power: Blessing of Full Food, This power will fill your food stores in warehouses and farms (this power will not fill warehouses that have the food resources turned off).
- New Ceres god Power: Lesser Destruction Food, this power will remove 1/2 of the food that is in your buildings.
- New Ceres god Power: Destruction of All Food, this power will remove all the food from your buildings.
- New Minerva god Power: Lesser Blessing of Knowledge, this power will grant 2 people a 1 level of education (so no education goes to basic education for instance).
- New Minerva god Power: Greater Blessing of Knowledge, this power will grant 10 people a 1 level of education (so no education goes to basic education for instance).
- New Minerva god Power: Strike Some Dumb, this power will reduce up to 1% of your population (round up) to no education. This power targets only educated people.
- New Minerva god Power: Strike Many Dumb, this power will reduce up to 3% of your population (round up) to no education. This power targets only educated people.
- Goods now have a mood score which is based on the % of the population their temples reach.
- The "Pantheon" tab in the stats screen now has information with reguards to how your city is doing with all of the gods.

Coming soon:

I obviously did not get to the bowyer, archery range, and archer this week. i will be working on them next week :) I also plan to work in the AI more, as well as some ease of use stuff next week.

Lastly I need to spend a great deal of time on the campaign mode, as I would like to have the first 5 or so levels in this month.

notes.title: Update 1.19c: Shopping and Market flow
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone!

So this took me quite a bit longer to rework than I thought it would. But the good news is that the system is MUCH better now, and after testing it quite a lot I think it is in a really good place now. Normally I am able to keep the "Starving" number to under 5% of my population (often much less) pretty much all the time. The shopping system is one of the (if not the) most important system in the game, and now that is in a much more refined state it will allow me to start to put in more of the desires as the game progresses.


Patch Notes:

- 100% rework of the unit Shopping AI. This should smooth out the process of markets getting your people what they actually want, without your people buying horrible choices unless there is no other options available.
- Markets now softcap their resources at 24 per resource.
- Markets now store 75 total units of resources up from 50.
- Added Market Upgrade: This upgrage costs 100 gold and 10 bricks. It gives the market 25 more storage capasity, as well as 1 more merchant slot. This upgrade seems to help smoothe
- Fixed a bug in the display for the market resources in which their capasities were not updating properly.
- Slightly increased the rate at which grapes grow.
- Units are a bit better at picking which market to shop at.
- Units can now buy more food at once.

notes.title: Update 1.19: Religion System
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone,

Ok so let me start with saying I didn't get it all in. So far I have two temples (one for Ceres and one for Minerva), more gods will come in time. Each home will want access to 1 god per level the home is. If they are access to more gods then they will be happy, and not enough will result in negative happiness. Currently the art for the temples is the same, however that will change as more art comes in.

What I did not get done was the gods giving benefits or exacting their wrath on your city :). I also have not finished the stats tab for religion, so for now it just says "Coming Soon". I hope to have the beginnings of the god's effects in by next Tuesday's patch.

Lastly later on, resources will be added that will boost the range of the religious buildings by 1 grid location (animals for sacrifice, wine, etc). 

Because education has become a bigger part of the game with this patch I have started 4 of your 9 starting units with a basic education. This should help you smooth out the early game, and give you some padding in order to get your people on the path to education.


Patch Notes:


- Added god: Ceres. Ceres will mostly affect farms and nature. When happy Ceres will provide your city with plant products, but while angry she will take out her wrath on these same areas.
- Added god: Minerva. Minerva will mostly affect the education and knowledge of your people. When happy she will help educate your people and and increase tech points, but while angry she may strike your people dumb or remove tech score. 
- Added Small Temple of Ceres. Has a max range of 3 grid locations in all directions. 1 + # of priests working is the calcuation for the distance.
- Added Small Temple of Minerva. Has a range of 3 grid locations in all directions.  1 + # of priests working is the calcuation for the distance.
- Each god's temples may affect each house 1 time (stacking tons of Ceres temples will not have any extra effect for example).
- For each housing level the residence will expect 1 more god to have a temple nearby (within the range of the building). Any additional gods with temples nearby will give happiness bonuses of +1 per.
- If the religious requirement is not met for your people they will get a happiness debuff of -1 per missing religious desire.
- Buildings have more upkeep now (about 20% more, thus less falling over...).
- Schools now educate people faster (about twice as fast).
- You now start with 4 Basic Educated people. This will help you get you started while your school(s) pump more more. Consider the use of these early educated people wisely...
- Newly immigrated units start with 4 grain rather than just 2. This should help them get to your city and have the opportunity to buy more before starving.
- Fixed a bug in tax collectors that could leave buildings as untaxable...


Whats coming soonish?

Bowyer (makes bows), Archery Range, and Archers. Are on the schedule for next week. I also plan to spend a pretty large chunk of time on the military units AI, as well as the enemy AI's

Further in the future:

Well with the religious system the placement of buildings has started to have an affect on your population not just your industry. This will continue to flesh out more and more which will in turn add more depth to the game. Eventually a desirability system will be added, in which proximity to things will raise or lower happiness as well.

I also want to slowly start adding in more negative events for low happiness (like tax collectors getting robbed, people setting fire to your buildings, etc).


I got a ton coming, I hope this helps to add to your experiences! I would really love to know what you guys think of this new system!

notes.title: Update 1.11: Trade System Update
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone,

So I spent the entire day on the Trade system, and I feel that it has come a long way. It is still only selling to the trade routes (the routes buying side), but I will get buying from routes in next week. The system is currently very similar to how Caesar 3's works in terms of features. From here we can improved it and grow it based on feedback :) The trade system is by no means finished, and I have lots of things I want to still do with it. But it is much improved now :)

Patch Notes:

- Trade now has a max per item per month. A month is currently designated as 30 days (later this will be the actual months of the year).
- Trade quantities resets every 30 days.
- Prices for trade items have been added to the stats->trade tab
- Because the Trade maximums reduce total possible trade, all trade values have been increased significantly.
- Optimized trade code, this will result is a minor cpu gains.
- Pottery now require 5 units clay up from 3. In turn it is now much more valuable in trade.
- Weapons now require 6 units of iron ore up from 3. In turn it is now much more valuable in trade.
- Merchants now no longer collect items that have fully traded in the current month.
- Merchants are now more likely to gather tradeable resources that the Tradeing Post has less of.
- Merchants now obey the reserve rules :)
- Fixed a bug in the Merchants AI where they would grab a totally random item, rather than the one they wanted...
- Base tax increased from 10% to 15%. 

If you guys are enjoying the game, or even just like the direction it is going, Please make sure to put up a positive review, as that will drive more traffic to the game!

Lastly, if you have a minute please tag the game with tags that you feel are appropriate, as this will also help drive traffic to the game :)

Thank you all for being a part of this game! I will be doing mostly feedback stuff tomorrow!

notes.title: Update 1.03: Happiness update and more!
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone,

Today's update is much larger in terms of actual gameplay additions and changes. This update give a much larger impact to the happiness system, and should start to create a larger skill curve for the game. There is also a substantial improvement to the upkeep system (the architects), which should smooth out the feature. Please keep in mind that spacing out architect offices is much better than clumping them together.


Patch Notes:

- I spent some time optimizing the Architect's AI. Please keep an eye out for any bugs, but also let me know if this has helped to make the upkeep system more bareable. More can be done if need be, but I want to take it 1 step at a time.
- The collapsed alert no longer pops up when a building is destroyed by attacking factions.
- The building info window now shows wages as white if they have no effect on happiness, green if they have a positive effect on happiness, and red if they have a negative effect on happiness.
- Wages above the starting value for each job will cause the citizen to be more happy. The higher the wage, the greater the effect. This effect takes place on payday (Friday).
- Wages below the starting value for each job will cause the citizen to be less happy. The Lower the wage, the worse the effect. This effect takes place on payday (Friday).
- Happiness now directly affects citizens Stamina (when Stamina gets low they have to go rest). For every 1 happiness they will gain 1% Stamina duration, also for every -1 happiness they will lose 1% Stamina duration.
- Constables will now stay 20% closer to their office. Constables also are now more likely to patrol closer to their office than the edge of their range.
- Constables now provide happiness to nearby citizens every so often. The tooltip had already said the do, but they did not. The title for the mood entry is "Feels Safe".
- Most mood entries (to see them select a unit and look in the unit info window) now stack, some will not stack on purpose for now.
- Barracks' standard now works properly when the game is paused.
- Rubble piles no longer have upkeep (this will also have a minor positive effect on architects).
- Weather sounds now properly stop playing when you exit the game.
- Data Windows should now pop up in front of all other windows when the open. This should make the moveable data windows feel less cumbersome.
- All Quanitity Bars (health, stamina, and upkeep at this time) have the % displayed on them now.
- All Quantity Bars (health, stamina, and upkeep at this time) now have a tooltip that say what they are keeping track of. This tooltip will improve at a later date.
- The immigrant spawn location should now be the closest pathable place on the map edge with reguards to your town hall (this was bugged before, please let me know if you see it acting strangely).
- The house(tent) building info window now shows occupants and you can click on them in order to select them.


Thank you all for your feedback! I am trying hard to address all of the feedback that is given, as well as prioritize it all so that you can see that I am working on it :) Keep the feedback coming! The more I get, the better the game can be!
